Mission Local said it could not independently verify the contribution. Per Crypto Briefing, Public First Action said none of the $3.5 million came from Anthropic, and Wiener said at a debate there was no Anthropic money in the race. (sources: Crypto Briefing https://cryptobriefing.com/anthropic-backed-group-3-million-scott-wiener/ [search summary, secondary]; Mission Local https://missionlocal.org/?p=876643 [search summary, secondary]; Mission Local https://missionlocal.org/?p=876609 [search summary, secondary])

items.label: GrowUSA (supports Wiener)
items.text: GrowUSA, the federal PAC of the San Francisco group GrowSF, supports Wiener. Mission Local reported $1.6 million spent backing Wiener and $1.3 million cash on hand at the end of September 2026. items.label: FPPC warning letter on late 24-hour contribution reports (2023)
items.text: The Fair Political Practices Commission's Enforcement Division issued a warning letter, FPPC No. 2022-00197, to Re-Elect Scott Wiener for State Senate 2020, Scott Wiener, and treasurer Stacy Owens. The letter is posted in the FPPC's April 11, 2023 enforcement-letter set; one search snippet gives the letter's own date as March 6, 2023. The FPPC PDF could not be fetched because fppc.ca.gov does not resolve from this session. Resolution: Closed with a warning letter. items.label: Sunshine Ordinance complaint against four supervisors; Ethics Commission found no violation (2011-2013)
items.text: The San Francisco Ethics Commission ruled on Ethics Complaint No. 02-12042 on September 23, 2013. The Sunshine Ordinance Task Force had referred the complaint to the Commission on April 2, 2012, and the Commission's records list the complainant as Pastor Gavin. By a 3-1 vote, the Commission determined that Supervisors David Chiu, Malia Cohen, Eric Mar and Scott Wiener did not commit a violation of the Sunshine Ordinance as alleged. Separately, the San Francisco Bay Guardian's archive (now hosted by 48hills) reported that in September 2011 the Task Force voted 8-0 that the same four supervisors violated the Sunshine Ordinance and the Brown Act. That vote concerned a Parkmerced redevelopment contract that the Land Use and Economic Development Committee, on which Mar, Wiener and Cohen served, recommended for approval. These sources do not confirm that the 2011 Task Force finding and the 2012 referral are the same matter. The Bay Guardian account was written by a Task Force advocate. Response: No statement from Wiener about the Task Force finding or the Ethics Commission ruling found. Searched: 'Scott Wiener SF Ethics Commission', 'Scott Wiener stipulation enforcement penalty committee' (sfethics.org and sf.gov), 'Sunshine Ordinance Task Force Parkmerced Wiener Chiu Mar Cohen Ethics Commission no violation', and 'Wiener responds Sunshine Ordinance Task Force finding Parkmerced 2011' (web search, including the Bay Guardian archive results). Resolution: Ethics Commission found no violation, 3-1, on September 23, 2013. items.label: Campaign AI chatbot parodying opponent withdrawn after criticism (August 2026)
items.text: In early August 2026, Wiener's congressional campaign launched ConnieChan.ai, an AI chatbot it described as a parody of opponent Connie Chan, and promoted it with billboards (KRON4; SFist, August 4, 2026). On August 6, 2026, the SF Standard reported that Chan's campaign had shared screenshots of chatbot replies about Chan's accent and citizenship. The Standard also reported that Nancy Pelosi, in a letter signed by several women elected officials, called the chatbot sexist and racist. The Wiener campaign said those replies appeared only after users repeatedly asked about Chan's accent, race, gender, appearance and citizenship, and it declined to give the Standard backend data to verify that claim. The SF Examiner and Axios also covered Pelosi's letter and the dispute. Response: Wiener said the chatbot was a parody meant to draw attention to Chan's record on housing and transit, and before the takedown the campaign said it was designed to focus on her record (SF Standard; SFist). On August 7, 2026, the campaign announced it would take down the chatbot and the billboards, saying the focus must remain on critical issues (SF Standard; SFist; Bay Area Reporter). NBC Bay Area reported that at a later debate with Chan, Wiener apologized to her and described the chatbot as a terrible mistake. Resolution: The chatbot and billboards were removed on August 7, 2026. No official complaint or agency finding was found. (sources: KRON4 https://www.kron4.com/news/politics/scott-wiener-launches-connie-chan-chatbot/amp [search summary, secondary]; SFist https://sfist.com/2026/08/04/scott-wiener-campaign-launches-ai-chatbot/ [search summary, secondary]; The San Francisco Standard https://sfstandard.com/2026/08/06/wiener-built-ai-chatbot-mock-chan-s-politics-pelosi-says-s-sexist-racist/ [search summary, secondary]; The San Francisco Standard https://sfstandard.com/2026/08/07/scott-wiener-takes-connie-chan-ai-chatbot-pushback-pelosi [search summary, secondary]; SFist https://sfist.com/2026/08/07/scott-wiener-takes-down-connie-chan-chatbot-after-backlash-from-pelosi-other-democrats/ [search summary, secondary]; Bay Area Reporter https://www.ebar.com/story/169066 [search summary, secondary]; San Francisco Examiner https://www.sfexaminer.com/news/politics/pelosi-posts-letter-slamming-wiener-chatbot-mimicking-chan/article_795e707e-7fe8-4fb7-95eb-4f329b7bc464.html [search summary, secondary]; Axios San Francisco https://www.axios.com/local/san-francisco/2026/08/11/sf-scott-wiener-connie-chan-pelosi-ai-chatbot [search summary, secondary]; NBC Bay Area https://www.nbcbayarea.com/news/local/chan-wiener-debate-sf-needs/4151924/ [search summary, secondary])

items.label: SB 35 (2017) streamlined approvals: unit counts
items.text: A preliminary analysis by the UC Berkeley Terner Center (February 2023) of local Annual Progress Report data for 2018-2021 found about 18,000 units proposed under SB 35. The data are self-reported by cities and counties, and Terner noted that verification was ongoing. Wiener's Senate office has stated that SB 35 streamlined approvals for about 12,000 homes in its first four years, nearly 75 percent of them below market rate. Mercy Housing, an affordable-housing developer that supported SB 423, described about 18,000 homes as built under SB 35. That conflicts with Terner's description of 18,000 units as proposed. items.label: SB 53 (2025) Transparency in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Act: implementation status
items.text: SB 53 was enacted in 2025, and law-firm alerts on its enactment are dated October 2025. Its core publication, incident-reporting, truthfulness and whistleblower obligations took effect January 1, 2026. Large frontier developers must publish safety frameworks and report critical safety incidents to Cal OES within 15 days, or within 24 hours where there is imminent risk of death or serious injury. The Attorney General enforces it, with civil penalties of up to $1 million per violation. Anonymized annual reports from OES and the Attorney General begin January 1, 2027. The law also creates CalCompute, a public computing cluster, within the Government Operations Agency. As of the most recent sources found (January and July 2026), no reporting was found on OES incident-reporting regulations or a reporting portal, on which developers have published frameworks, on any Attorney General enforcement, or on CalCompute's build-out. No court challenge to SB 53 was found in these searches. (sources: Morrison Foerster (law firm) https://www.mofo.com/resources/insights/251001-california-enacts-ai-safety-transparency-regulation-tfaia-sb-53 [search summary, secondary]; Kilpatrick Townsend (law firm) https://ktslaw.com/insights/alert/2025/10/california-enacts-the-transparency-in-frontier-artificial-intelligence-act-sb-53 [search summary, secondary]; National Law Review https://natlawreview.com/article/californias-sb-53-understanding-obligations-effect-now-and-2027 [search summary, secondary]; METR (AI evaluation nonprofit) https://metr.org/notes/2026-01-29-frontier-ai-safety-regulations/ [search summary, secondary])

items.label: State budgets as Senate Budget and Fiscal Review Committee chair (2024-25 and 2025-26 cycles)
items.text: Wiener chaired the Senate Budget Committee during the 2024-25 and 2025-26 budget cycles. When he was appointed, EBAR reported a projected 2024-25 deficit of about $68 billion. With Senate Leader Mike McGuire, he presented an early-action plan described as cutting about $17 billion, and the Senate voted on deficit-reduction measures on April 11, 2024. A Senate press release records the Legislature passing the 2024-25 budget plan. In an October 2025 column, Wiener states that he led the Senate's 2025-26 budget work and helped close a $12 billion deficit. That is his own statement and has not been checked against LAO or Department of Finance figures. (sources: Bay Area Reporter (EBAR) https://www.ebar.com/story/73868 [search summary, secondary]; The Bond Buyer https://www.bondbuyer.com/news/california-senators-propose-deficit-shrinking-budget-cuts [search summary, secondary]; California State Senate, Office of Senate Leader Mike McGuire https://sd02.senate.ca.gov/news/senate-leader-mike-mcguire-budget-chair-wiener-issue-statements-legislature-passing-2024-25 [search summary, primary]; Richmond Sunset News (column written by Scott Wiener) https://richmondsunsetnews.com/2025/10/08/state-senate-scott-wiener-5/ [search summary, primary])

items.label: SB 79 (2025-26 session), transit-oriented housing
items.text: SB 79, by Wiener, was signed on October 10, 2025 and took effect July 1, 2026. It allows multi-story multifamily housing near qualifying transit stops in specified urban counties, including San Francisco. (sources: KQED https://www.kqed.org/news/12059533/newsom-signs-ambitious-bill-to-boost-housing-density-near-public-transit [search summary, secondary]; Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_Senate_Bill_79 [search summary, secondary])

items.label: SB 79 implementation in San Francisco and litigation
items.text: San Francisco adopted a local alternative plan under SB 79 through Ordinance 082-26 (Board File 260132), which the Board adopted on May 5, 2026 and which was signed on May 8, 2026. The city states that as a result no San Francisco parcel is subject to SB 79's default provisions, with some exemptions running to January 2032. HCD's letter of July 1, 2026 found that the ordinance and plan substantially comply with SB 79, on the condition that the city not enforce Planning Code Section 207.11(b)(5). The California Housing Defense Fund, Californians for Homeownership and YIMBY Law, all housing advocacy groups, sued San Francisco and HCD to void the plan and strike that provision. The status of that suit was not found. No count of units approved under SB 79 was found as of November 2026. (sources: California Department of Housing and Community Development https://www.hcd.ca.gov/sites/default/files/docs/planning-and-community/HAU/san-francisco-sb79-in-070126.pdf [search summary, primary]; San Francisco Planning Department https://sfplanning.org/project/senate-bill-79-implementation-san-francisco [search summary, primary]; City and County of San Francisco (Ordinance 082-26) https://media.api.sf.gov/documents/o0082-26.pdf [search summary, primary]; California Housing Defense Fund (advocacy group) https://calhdf.org/?p=19491 [search summary, secondary]; Davis Vanguard https://davisvanguard.org/2026/07/california-housing-law-sb79-2/ [search summary, secondary])

items.label: SB 627 (2025-26 session), No Secret Police Act
items.text: SB 627, by Wiener, restricts face coverings for law enforcement officers. Several sources say it was signed in September 2025 and took effect January 1, 2026; one source gives conflicting 2026 dates. In February 2026, U.S. District Judge Christina Snyder issued a preliminary injunction against the mask ban as applied to federal officers in United States v. California. She found that it likely discriminates against federal officers because state police were exempt. She declined to enjoin SB 805 or SB 627's other provisions. Wiener introduced follow-up legislation to add state officers, and its outcome was not found. The California Globe reported that the Ninth Circuit later stayed the entire act. The date of that stay and its current status were not confirmed. (sources: Local News Matters (Bay City News) https://localnewsmatters.org/2026/02/12/wiener-moves-to-salvage-no-secret-police-law-after-federal-judge-halts-enforcement/ [search summary, secondary]; KQED https://www.kqed.org/news/12072927/after-us-judge-blocks-californias-ice-mask-ban-scott-wiener-says-he-will-make-it-enforceable [search summary, secondary]; Bloomberg Government https://news.bgov.com/bloomberg-government-news/enforcement-of-californias-ice-agent-mask-ban-blocked-by-judge [search summary, secondary]; California Globe https://californiaglobe.com/fr/ninth-circuit-blocks-californias-entire-no-secret-police-act-in-major-win-for-trump-doj/ [search summary, secondary]; Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Secret_Police_Act [search summary, secondary])

items.label: SB 253 (2023-24 session), Climate Corporate Data Accountability Act
items.text: SB 253 requires large companies doing business in California to report greenhouse gas emissions. Wiener's news page carries a headline about the governor announcing he would sign it; authorship and the signing date need confirming at leginfo. In late February 2026, CARB approved initial regulations. Sources conflict on the deadline for the first Scope 1 and 2 reports: August 10, 2026 in some, and November 10, 2026 in a later law-firm note on OAL approval. Scope 3 reporting begins in 2027. The Ninth Circuit heard argument on January 9, 2026 in the challenge to the denial of a preliminary injunction. It stayed the companion law SB 261 (not Wiener's) but not SB 253. No merits ruling was found as of these sources. (sources: Scott Wiener campaign site (news page) https://www.scottwiener.com/news [search summary, primary]; Cooley (law firm) https://www.cooley.com/news/insight/2026/2026-01-26-californias-sb-253-and-sb-261-developments-and-litigation [search summary, secondary]; Proskauer (law firm) https://www.proskauer.com/alert/californias-climate-disclosure-laws-initial-implementing-regulations-approved [search summary, secondary]; Vinson & Elkins (law firm) https://www.velaw.com/insights/oal-approves-carbs-initial-regulation-locking-in-november-10-2026-sb-253-reporting-deadline/ [search summary, secondary]; Winston Taylor (law firm) https://www.winstontaylor.com/insights/ninth-circuit-pauses-california-climate-risk-reporting-law-lets-climate-corporate-data-accountability-act-proceed [search summary, secondary])

items.label: SB 4 (2023-24 session), Affordable Housing on Faith and Higher Education Lands Act
items.text: SB 4, by Wiener, was signed in October 2023. It streamlines approval of qualifying, generally 100 percent affordable, housing on land owned by religious institutions and nonprofit colleges, and sunsets January 1, 2036. A Terner Center estimate puts about 171,000 acres as potentially eligible. That is an estimate of eligible land, not of units approved or built. HCD issued an SB 4 fact sheet in April 2026. No count of projects or units approved under SB 4 was found. (sources: Office of Senator Scott Wiener https://sd11.senate.ca.gov/node/1215 [search summary, primary]; Terner Center for Housing Innovation, UC Berkeley https://ternercenter.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/Faith-Based-Housing-Updated-October-2023.pdf [search summary, secondary]; California Department of Housing and Community Development https://www.hcd.ca.gov/sites/default/files/docs/planning-and-community/aff-hsg-faith-higher-ed-sb-4.pdf [search summary, primary]; Liebert Cassidy Whitmore (law firm) https://www.lcwlegal.com/news/sb-4-enacts-affordable-housing-on-faith-and-higher-education-lands-act-of-2023/ [search summary, secondary])

items.label: AI regulation at October 2026 debate
items.text: KQED reported that at the October 2026 debate both Chan and Wiener said AI should be regulated, including independent safety checks and human oversight, and that AI companies should not be left to regulate themselves. Debate coverage also reported that Chan described the final, amended version of Wiener's AI law as watered down and questioned who shaped the amendments; one search summary flagged the attribution of that remark as unclear, so it needs checking against the articles. No statement from Chan specifically on legally required safety disclosures or incident reporting by frontier developers (SB 53, SB 1047 or a federal equivalent) was found. (sources: KQED https://www.kqed.org/news/12104381/san-francisco-is-ground-zero-for-ai-how-would-congressional-candidates-push-for-regulation [search summary, secondary]; Mission Local https://missionlocal.org/2026/10/scott-wiener-connie-chan-ai-debate/ [search summary, secondary]; The San Francisco Standard https://sfstandard.com/2026/10/01/five-takeaways-congressional-debate-wiener-chan-clash-ai-regulation/ [search summary, secondary])

items.label: AI regulatory framework
items.text: In 2026 coverage, Chan said Congress should establish a framework for AI consumer safety and consumer protection, and tied her support for a national pause on new large AI data centers to Congress first setting rules on AI's economic, environmental and safety effects. Her campaign spokesperson listed worker and union input and protections against AI-driven job displacement and surveillance as priorities. (sources: Mission Local https://missionlocal.org/2026/08/sf-congress-candidates-ai-data-centers/ [search summary, secondary]; KQED https://www.kqed.org/news/12104381/san-francisco-is-ground-zero-for-ai-how-would-congressional-candidates-push-for-regulation [search summary, secondary])

items.label: Tech monopolies (April 2026 questionnaire)
items.text: In an April 2026 Mission Local candidate questionnaire on tech, AI and crypto, Chan said she favors breaking up monopolies and supports more competition among platforms, and Mission Local summarized her as favoring limits on the power of tech monopolies. The answer did not specifically address prohibiting self-preferencing; the self-preferencing remarks in that article were attributed to Saikat Chakrabarti. Wiener did not take part in that questionnaire. No statement from Chan on SB 1074, the BASED Act or federal self-preferencing bills was found. (sources: Mission Local https://missionlocal.org/2026/04/sf-congress-connie-chan-saikat-chakrabarti-scott-wiener-tech-ai-crypto/ [search summary, secondary])

items.label: Resolution opposing SB 79 (2025)
items.text: In July 2025, Supervisor Chan introduced a Board of Supervisors resolution opposing SB 79, saying the bill undercut San Francisco's years-long community process for its Housing Element. The Board rejected the resolution 7-4 at its July 22, 2025 meeting. A 48hills preview listed Supervisors Chyanne Chen and Jackie Fielder as co-sponsors and said the non-binding resolution urged the Legislature to defeat the bill. (sources: San Francisco Examiner https://www.sfexaminer.com/news/housing/how-california-sb-79-may-increase-sf-housing-height-limits/article_f63e1c94-292d-4519-8e97-46ba0aba190f.html [search summary, secondary]; 48hills https://newsletters.48hills.org/big-tests-for-the-supes-this-week-budget-rent-controlled-housing-rv-ban/ [search summary, secondary])

items.label: Vote on SF Family Zoning Plan (2025)
items.text: In December 2025 the Board of Supervisors approved Mayor Daniel Lurie's Family Zoning Plan, a local rezoning, 7-4; Chan voted no, along with Supervisors Shamann Walton, Chyanne Chen and Jackie Fielder. She said the plan lacked protections against displacement of tenants and small businesses, and had proposed amendments with Supervisor Chen. This was a local zoning action, not a state law, so it is not mapped to the question. (sources: Local News Matters (Bay City News) https://localnewsmatters.org/2025/12/03/sf-supes-pass-family-zoning-plan/ [search summary, secondary]; The San Francisco Standard https://sfstandard.com/2025/12/15/moderate-political-group-attacks-supervisors-who-voted-lurie-s-upzoning-plan/ [search summary, secondary])

items.label: SB 79 (2025), transit-oriented housing
items.text: Wiener authored SB 79 (2025), which sets state standards allowing taller, denser housing within roughly a half mile of major transit stops and adds a Transit Oriented Development chapter to the Government Code. The Senate gave final approval 21-8 after an Assembly floor vote; Governor Gavin Newsom signed it on October 10, 2025, and it took effect July 1, 2026, with an option for cities to adopt a state-approved local alternative plan. (sources: Office of Senator Scott Wiener (California State Senate) https://sd11.senate.ca.gov/node/1399 [search summary, primary]; The San Francisco Standard https://sfstandard.com/2025/10/10/newsom-sb-79-housing-transit/ [search summary, secondary]; Streetsblog California https://cal.streetsblog.org/2025/10/10/newsom-signs-sb-79-legislation-to-spur-housing-production-near-transit [search summary, secondary]; Coblentz Patch Duffy & Bass LLP https://www.coblentzlaw.com/?p=10896 [search summary, secondary])

items.label: Author of SB 79
items.text: As author of SB 79, Wiener carried the state law that permits higher-density housing near major transit stops under state standards that apply even where local zoning is more restrictive (subject to a state-approved local alternative plan), and described its enactment as a historic step toward addressing the root cause of California's affordability crisis. (sources: Office of Senator Scott Wiener (California State Senate) https://sd11.senate.ca.gov/node/1399 [search summary, primary]; KQED https://www.kqed.org/news/12059533/newsom-signs-ambitious-bill-to-boost-housing-density-near-public-transit [search summary, secondary])

items.label: Position on Prop 40 (billionaire tax)
items.text: In a May 2026 SF Standard interview, Wiener said he does not support the statewide billionaire tax initiative and that a one-time wealth tax is not the best approach. The Intercept reported in May 2026 that he said he opposed the measure after its backers announced they had enough signatures to qualify it, and Mission Local reported in September 2026 that he opposes Proposition 40. (sources: The San Francisco Standard https://sfstandard.com/2026/05/04/power-play-scott-wiener-tax/ [search summary, secondary]; The Intercept https://theintercept.com/2026/05/14/scott-wiener-billionaire-tax-california-house-race/ [search summary, secondary]; Mission Local https://missionlocal.org/2026/09/scott-wiener-connie-chan-who-would-you-tax-more/ [search summary, secondary])
